stage.name: OpenMAIC in 5 Minutes
stage.description: A light, friendly first look at OpenMAIC for new students and teachers.

generatedAgentConfigs.name: Ms. Lane
generatedAgentConfigs.persona: Ms. Lane is a warm, patient teacher who explains things in short plain sentences and always checks that nothing feels confusing yet. She likes small everyday examples and never makes anyone feel silly for asking a basic question. She keeps the pace calm and cheerful, like a friendly first-day guide.

generatedAgentConfigs.name: Mia
generatedAgentConfigs.persona: Mia is a curious classmate who asks the very question you were about to ask. She likes to try buttons first and figure things out by clicking around. She says short, friendly things and is happy to be wrong out loud.

generatedAgentConfigs.name: Leo
generatedAgentConfigs.persona: Leo is an easy-going classmate who sums things up in plain words after a page. He asks practical questions about what to click next. He is a bit cautious and likes knowing he cannot break anything.

actions.text: Hi there, I'm Ms. Lane, your teacher. With OpenMAIC, you type a topic you want to learn, and a few minutes later you have a whole class.
It comes with slides, a teacher who explains them, classmates who learn with you, quiz questions and pages you can click.
And this class? It was made exactly that way.

elements.content: What is OpenMAIC?

Type a topic. A few minutes later,
you have a whole class.
The class you are in right now was made this way.

actions.text: So what do you type first? A short topic is enough, like photosynthesis.

A learner could write: help me understand compound interest with everyday examples. A teacher might say: a fifteen-minute lesson on the Pythagorean theorem for 8th graders, with one practice question.
Already have a handout? Click the paperclip at the bottom left of the input box, upload it, and say: turn this handout into a class.

actions.text: Want to change something? Just say it in the chat on the left.
Like: the text is too small. Add a practice question to page 3. Explain it more simply.
At the top right, Learn is for taking the class, and Edit lets you change the text, the pictures and what I say yourself.
